chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
“There is no hadd punishment for one regarding whom there is no hadd punishment.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The meaning of this report is that if a person were to accuse an insane man or an insane woman of fornication, the hadd would not be obligatory upon him, because if the insane person were to accuse him, there would be no hadd upon the insane person. We shall clarify that later in the chapter on qadhf, if Allah wills.

key_terms.بَابِ ٱلْقَذْفِ: the chapter dealing with false accusation of fornication
key_terms.حَدَّ: prescribed legal punishment in Islamic law
key_terms.مَجْنُونًا: an insane man, not legally accountable for hadd
key_terms.مَجْنُونَةً: an insane woman, not legally accountable for hadd
key_terms.ٱلْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith being explained

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment for qadhf apply when a person accuses an insane person?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle concerning hadd punishment and those to whom it applies. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains that it refers to the case of falsely accusing an insane person of fornication, for the hadd of qadhf does not apply there because the insane person is not legally subject to hadd.
